_comment: Hosts whose presence on a page is a fact worth reporting, grouped by what
they are for. JSON and not a module: background/fine-print.js is loaded
through the offscreen door and this file is fetched beside it, so neither
is in the service worker's boot graph, which tools/test-worker-imports.mjs
holds to a hard byte ceiling.
Suffix matching, so 'www.google-analytics.com' and any regional variant of
it are one entry. A host being here is not an accusation: analytics on a
site is normal and often disclosed. What the check reports is that the page
called it, and whether the policy pages that ought to name it exist.
Deliberately short. A list of nine hundred hosts is a maintenance burden
that goes stale in a month and turns a QA finding into a blocklist
argument. These are the ones a tester will actually meet.

analytics.label: Analytics
analytics.why: Records what visitors do. Needs consent in the EU and a line in the privacy policy.

advertising.label: Advertising
advertising.why: Builds a profile of the visitor across sites. Consent is not optional in most jurisdictions.

social.label: Social embeds
social.why: A widget from another company, loaded into your page, that can see the visitor.

support.label: Support and chat
support.why: A live chat widget is a third party reading the page and often the visitor's details.

payments.label: Payments
payments.why: Expected on a shop, and worth naming: the visitor's card details pass through it.
